news.2026-11-22-algerie-maroc-frontiere-: Algeria-Morocco: Algerian army says it shot dead two Moroccans on the border, closed since 1994, the third deadly incident this year

Algeria's Defence Ministry announced on Saturday, 21 November, that border guards had killed two Moroccan nationals the day before, described as drug traffickers, near Naâma, facing eastern Morocco. Rabat has not given its version. It is at least the third such case in 2026 [1][2][3].

According to the statement, a border guard detachment of the 2nd Military Region "neutralised" the two men on Friday, 20 November, in the Naâma military sector, after they refused to comply with orders [1][3].

One of them was identified from his identity card: Khelifi Laid, born in Oulad Sidi Abdelhakem, in Jerada province; the other was not named [2][3]. More than 50 kilos of processed cannabis were seized, according to the press [4].
On 28 January, the Algerian army had announced the death of three Moroccans near Béchar; on 27 February, two more at Béni Ounif, each time citing the fight against drug trafficking [2][5].
The land border has been closed since 1994, and Algiers broke off diplomatic relations with Rabat in August 2021 [2][3].
The key point: every incident on the border is read through the Western Sahara dispute, which has pitted the two neighbours against each other for decades [3].

On 17 November in Rabat, the US ambassador to the UN, Mike Waltz, reaffirmed Washington's support for Morocco's autonomy plan and urged the Algiers-backed Polisario Front to "choose peace", just as the withdrawal of the UN mission (MINURSO) begins after 35 years [6][7]. For now, the only sources on the shooting are the Algerian statement and the press reporting it [2][3].
Between these two Maghreb neighbours, the closed border rules out any trade by road and separates families; each deadly incident makes a reopening even less likely.
